bull_bear.body: Prioritizing capex for LNG and keg capacity; maintaining net cash position (INR275cr available); no dividend or buyback mentioned; focus on organic growth and strategic order execution
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Keg volume ramp-up delayed vs internal targets; LNG station rollout slower than policy potential; execution risk on ITER project (long duration); global trade policy shifts (US tariffs); competitive pressure from Chinese players in kegs (mitigated by antidumping duties)
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident, forward-looking, and execution-focused; emphasized technological leadership, global approvals, and policy tailwinds; tone on LNG and kegs is bullish; ITER and CO2 battery framed as strategic differentiators, not one-offs
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The INR28,000cr Q2FY26 keg order (pre-announced) is likely a cumulative pipeline value, not a single order — indicating strong pre-commitments from global brewers; ITER’s 200 CTS panels represent a multi-year, high-margin, repeatable workstream beyond the INR145cr order; CO2 battery order from Italy signals export-ready clean energy tech, not just domestic
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Strong Balance Sheet (Net Debt Free)" with net debt defined in the deck as "[Gross Debt incl. short term] Less [Cash & Bank, FDR & Mutual Fund]", all formulae stated to be as per the definition in the RHP.
- "Availability of Approx Rs 331 Cr Free Cash"; net cash/bank balance is higher than Mar'26 despite payment of dividend, helped by an increase in advances from customers and realization of contract assets/trade receivables.
- Growth and capex are funded internally: "Debt-free and strong net worth; Savli plant funded from internal accruals" and "Strong liquidity and robust operational cash flow to support growth & capex".
- Treasury is run for carry rather than debt reduction: finance cost is higher because of "not liquidating the Long Term Mutual Fund to save taxes and utilizing the fund based limit to get benefit of differential gain of around 0.75% in earning vs cost of funds", so the deck argues there is "no increase in Net Finance cost in real terms".
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Global leader in customised cryogenic equipment; among the largest cryogenic tank manufacturers in the world
- Complete end-to-end capability: design, engineering, manufacturing, installation and after-sales service
- Diversified customer base of 590+ clients across industrial gas, LNG, scientific and beverage segments
- Export-oriented manufacturing at Kandla Special Economic Zone providing logistics and duty advantages for international business
- International commercial infrastructure: subsidiaries and service centres in Brazil, marketing offices in Europe
- Backward and forward integration with group companies contributing 10% of revenues
- Robust financial profile: Debt-Equity of 0.06x (FY26), interest coverage of 38.04x, RONW of 23.08%
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Customer concentration — Top 10 customers contributed 51% of FY26 revenues, creating sensitivity to individual customer demand cycles.
- Export revenue / geopolitical concentration — Export revenues comprised 59% of FY26 revenues, exposing the Company to anti-dumping investigations, trade barriers, shipping disruptions and currency volatility in key export markets, as well as trade-policy shifts.
- Manufacturing continuity — Dependence on four principal manufacturing facilities in India; disruption at a facility could affect production, mitigated by preventive maintenance, business continuity planning and multi-plant redundancy.
- Input cost volatility — Exposure to steel, stainless steel and energy price fluctuations; mitigated by strategic procurement, vendor diversification and selective pass-through pricing in contracts.
- Order book execution risk — Orders are subject to revision, delay or cancellation, which could affect revenue visibility from the order backlog.
- Demand cyclicality from long equipment life cycles — Major operators periodically relocate existing equipment rather than buy new, deferring procurement and creating episodic demand troughs.
- Commodity price and policy sensitivity of LNG/hydrogen demand — Future demand for LNG and hydrogen equipment is sensitive to commodity prices and government policy continuity (e.g. India's gas-in-energy-mix and Green Hydrogen Mission targets), both of which carry structural uncertainty.
- Competitive pricing pressure — Increasing competition from low-cost manufacturers in emerging markets offering aggressive pricing on standardised equipment categories.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Self-described as the "World's leading provider of customized cryogenic equipment" with "Over 30 years of experience in design, manufacturing and installation of cryogenic equipment" and, under Key Strengths, the "Largest supplier of cryogenic equipment in India".
- Global reach: "5000+ customers across 100+ countries", 3 countries with INOXCVA operations and 30+ sales & service support locations; key export geographies listed as US, Europe, Saudi Arabia, Brazil, Korea, UAE, Australia and Bangladesh.
- Entry barrier claimed from a third-party source: "Stringency related to design, manufacturing and the number of regulations in the cryogenic equipment segment is a barrier to entry" (footnoted to Crisil report Nov23), reinforced by approvals including ASME U & R Stamp, DOT 39, EN 13458/EN 13530, CE, IATF 16949, FSSC 22000, ISO 3824-Part 2 and AS9100 D Aerospace.
- Stated vision: "To be the world's best integrated cryogenic solutions enterprise with a leadership position across products and markets, exceeding customer and stakeholder expectations", supported by six growth pillars including "introducing products ahead of demand".
- Resilience framing of "Multiple Geographies, Multiple Sectors, Multiple Products" spanning "Steel to Space", "Healthcare to Hydrogen" and "Paper To Power".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Order intake] "Highest ever Order booking" of Rs 532 Cr in Q1FY27 (Actual orders received Rs 532 Cr vs Rs 415 Cr in Q1FY26, +28.4%), which the deck notes "includes high value order of Rs 217 Cr from US major private Aerospace Co. (IG)"; the Q1FY26 base included an ITER France order of Rs 146 Cr for CTS Repair (CSD). Q1FY27 order mix: IG 72%, LNG 16%, CSD 10%, Other 2%.
- [Aerospace / space] Secured AS9100 Aerospace Certification serving aviation, space and defence; an additional order from a US space company for large size (1000M3) tanks and a high-value repeat order from a global aerospace company; the 2024 milestone records an order for largest size (1500M3) tanks in the IG segment from a US space company. The deck also details INOXCVA's role in ISRO test-facility and launchpad systems.
- [Big science] Secured an order for 22 Nos of cryogenic modules for CERN's HL-LHC project, plus an additional ITER order for installation of Cryo & Warm line and refurbishment of the Lower Cryostat Thermal Shield; ITER First Plasma is cited as expected in 2035 and India is described as developing a 25-year fusion roadmap with two new tokamak machines before an Indian DEMO in the late 2040s.
- [Partnerships] Agreement with Wayout to explore a freshwater infra system for the Asian market, and a collaboration with ITMBU for skill development in orbital welding and semiconductor industries; India's semiconductor push (ISM) is flagged as an adjacent opportunity.
- [Headwind stated] "Sales were marginally lower on YoY basis primarily due to ongoing logistics disruptions arising from the geopolitical situation involving Iran and the Gulf region"; other income also fell 14.7% as forex gain dropped to Rs 0.3 Cr from Rs 2.9 Cr.

business.body: INOX India Ltd (INOXCVA) designs, engineers, manufactures, delivers and installs vacuum-insulated cryogenic equipment and systems for the storage, distribution and transfer of cryogens (helium, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, LNG and more) across a temperature range of 2-200 Kelvin. The Company operates through four divisions - Industrial Gas, LNG, Cryo Scientific and Stainless Steel Kegs - serving 590+ customers spanning industrial gas producers, LNG operators, space agencies, healthcare institutions and beverage companies across more than 100 countries.
business.title: What they do

business.body:

- **Cryo Scientific Division (CSD):** Superconductivity systems, Liquid helium distribution systems, Cryogenic propulsion systems, Space simulation chambers, ISRO-related infrastructure, ITER fusion project components (cryolines, Vacuum Vessel Thermal Shield repair)
- **Stainless Steel KEG Division:** Premium returnable stainless steel beverage kegs (in collaboration with Supermonte Group, Italy)

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Establishing global leadership in modular mini-LNG terminal technology, having delivered projects in Scotland and Antigua and now executing a third major contract in The Bahamas as a regional clean energy hub
- Building capabilities in small-scale LNG (SS-LNG) projects for remote industrial locations, island nations and off-grid power generation, and executing projects across multiple geographies
- Continuing to build opportunities in emerging segments such as hydrogen storage, long-duration energy storage and advanced cryogenic applications aligned with the clean energy transition
- Positioning as a critical enabler of India's hydrogen economy under the National Green Hydrogen Mission through liquid hydrogen cryogenic tanks, transfer systems and distribution infrastructure
- Extending addressable market into stainless steel beverage kegs (division launched FY25) in collaboration with Supermonte Group, Italy, targeting global beverage producers phasing out single-use containers
- Expanding global engagement through participation in international industry forums and customer collaborations in LNG infrastructure, marine fuel systems and small-scale LNG applications
- Deepening presence in emerging cryogenic applications - hydrogen storage, semiconductor-grade ultra-high-purity gas equipment, and CO2/liquid air energy storage systems
- Dividend of Rs 2/- per equity share of Rs 2/- face value (100%), as recommended by the Board, to be declared at the 49th AGM (23rd June 2026) and paid out of the Company's profits.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Targeted investments in advanced automation and precision fabrication strengthened manufacturing capabilities during FY26, enhancing throughput and ensuring adherence to global quality standards, positioning the Company's facilities as competitive export hubs for complex, high-value infrastructure. The Kandla (KASEZ) export-oriented facility was honoured with the Award for Excellence in Export 2024-25. Capital expenditure allocated toward enhancement of sustainability and safety measures represented 5.65% of total capex in FY26 (6.29% in FY25), per BRSR Principle 2 disclosure.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Growth in air separation plants, semiconductor manufacturing, the hydrogen economy and advanced industrial processes continues to create strong demand for cryogenic storage, transportation and handling solutions
- India's industrial expansion and rising investments in electronics manufacturing, specialty chemicals, steel, pharmaceuticals and healthcare are accelerating the need for reliable cryogenic infrastructure
- Global energy transition initiatives are driving increasing demand for hydrogen, ammonia and other clean energy carriers, creating new opportunities for technologically advanced cryogenic equipment
- Increasing adoption of cryogenic solutions in healthcare, biotechnology, dairy and industrial applications is supporting strong demand for liquid nitrogen containers, liquid cylinders and other standardised equipment
- Growing investments in semiconductor fabrication facilities, renewable energy infrastructure and advanced manufacturing hubs are expanding the scope for engineered cryogenic storage systems
- Government target to raise natural gas' share of India's energy mix from ~6% to 15% by 2030 is accelerating LNG import terminal expansion, City Gas Distribution network growth and LNG fuelling corridor development, expected to significantly increase demand for LNG storage, transportation and regasification systems
- Gradual transition of heavy vehicles towards LNG power (longer range, lower emissions, improved efficiency versus diesel) is expected to drive strong demand for cryogenic fuel tanks and semi-trailers
- The marine sector is increasingly adopting LNG-powered vessels to comply with environmental regulations, creating new opportunities for marine fuel tanks and related LNG infrastructure
- Steel, mining, cement and heavy manufacturing industries are increasingly evaluating LNG as a cleaner fuel alternative for logistics and industrial applications
- EBITDA margin reflects operating leverage benefits on a higher revenue base alongside disciplined cost management
- PBT growth supported by higher operating income and declining finance costs driven by the Company's strong balance sheet
- Order Inflow in FY26 was Rs. 1,685 Cr, up 9.9% YoY, reflecting sustained global demand across the Company's addressable segments
- Order Backlog as at end-FY26 stood at Rs. 1,514 Cr, split approximately 49% Industrial Gas, 28% LNG and 22% Cryo Scientific Division, providing visibility on near-term revenue
- Sold 70+ LNG semi-trailers during the financial year, strengthening presence in LNG logistics solutions
- Executing a third major LNG contract in The Bahamas featuring ten vacuum-insulated tanks with 15,000 cubic metres combined capacity, serving as a regional clean energy hub
- Secured a prestigious order from Cochin Shipyard for 6 units of 800 m3 Marine Fuel Gas Tanks for CMA CGM container vessels, marking entry into Indian shipyards and the largest marine tanks executed by the Company
- Secured export orders for LNG storage tanks, marine fuel gas tanks and LNG infrastructure projects across Asia, Africa and South America
- First-of-a-kind order for largest-size (10 units) horizontal LOX storage tanks under manufacture for a space research company
- First-of-a-kind order for a vertical LH2 storage tank (90kl) from a European customer for a semiconductor/electronics factory
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: INOX India delivered strong Q1FY26 growth with 16.7% revenue rise, driven by breakthrough orders in ultra-high-purity ammonia containers and India’s first CO2 battery storage system, while LNG and keg segments show scalable momentum; the company’s diversified high-margin product portfolio and strategic capex expansion position it to capture India’s clean energy transition and global industrial supply chain reshoring.

open.item: Company reiterated it is a consistent dividend-paying company and will consider a dividend at year-end, having a comfortable net cash of Rs.191 crore.

Management flagged US tariffs (35%) as a tricky, changing issue but expects only a slight, not substantial, impact given US is ~10-12% of revenue and tariff applies only to the steel component of cylinders.

ISRO/space tender for the third launch pad (total ~Rs.4,000 crore, cryogenic ~15-20% of it) expected to be out around December/early next year; company sees a better chance having done the second launch pad.

Secured global approval from Heineken (plus AB InBev already done); Carlsberg and Asahi audits scheduled for September/October, expected to unlock keg volume ramp; new distributors appointed in UK, Germany and US.
Company secured its first-of-its-kind Australia order (~Rs.21 crore) for oxygen/nitrogen/CO2 IMO containers with a challenging sub-6-month delivery timeline, committed to meeting it.

Executing first Highview Power (long-duration storage) project, delivery expected by end January/February; management expects more of Highview's 4-5 pipeline projects (to be completed by 2030) to start flowing from the beginning of next year.
open.promised: delivery Jan-Feb; new orders early CY26 text

open.item: Company is targeting at least 100,000 beverage kegs sold this year, with a vision to be 3-4x current size in 3-4 years.
Savli plant did ~Rs.200 crore last year and is planned for Rs.300-350 crore this year, with stabilization expected in about 6 months to 1 year; 150+ tanks currently under construction.
Company is qualified with Blue Energy (India's largest LNG-tank OEM) and expects to supply substantial equipment this year; mini LNG terminal order flow expected from the beginning of next year.
Company targets FY26 capex of around Rs.80 crore, mainly for Kandla facility expansion (1,500 cubic-meter vessels) plus Kalol and Savli.
Industrial Gas segment is expected to grow around 15%-17% in FY26 (8-10% conventional plus 5-6% from new products).
Management targets FY26 total revenue growth of about 18%-20%.
Company delivered 9 tanks (50-200 KL) to a US semiconductor customer and won an order from Tata's semiconductor complex in Assam to be supplied in FY26.
Existing capacity implies peak revenue potential of ~Rs.1,200-1,300 crore at Kalol/Kandla plus Rs.300-500 crore from Savli over 1-2 years (~Rs.1,800 crore max on current capacity).
Company secured an ITER Cryostat Thermal Shield order worth ~Rs.145 crore, with ~90% fabrication in-house and the project expected to span nearly 2 years.
Company aims to scale LNG fuel-tank capability up to 10x over the next few years, anticipating a need for 30,000-40,000 fuel tanks in 3-5 years.
As leading conglomerates set up 5 MTPA green hydrogen production capacity by 2030, ~20% of each project's revenue (liquid hydrogen storage/transport) is the addressable opportunity for INOX.
Company is augmenting its Kalol serial LNG fuel-tank line to ~500-600 tanks/month (5,000-6,000 units/year) at a capex of Rs.5-6 crore, and is evaluating a much larger facility.
Received DOT 39 approval for A12, helium and R32 gas cylinders in the US, opening an incremental market of 5-6 lakh additional cylinders.

Delivered India's first ultra-high-purity ammonia ISO containers (2 of an 11-unit order delivered, 9 in pipeline) with an additional 10 units under construction; expects demand in the hundreds in coming years.

verdicts.item: Management expects to maintain EBITDA margins in the 21%-25% range, slightly better on mega projects like Bahamas but overall in-line.
verdicts.note: 'EBITDA was INR89 crores' on 'revenue of INR352 crores' — margin tracking within the guided range; FY26 ongoing. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Company started construction of a new cryo shop at Savli, spending around Rs.80 crores on new capex (machinery + building); Savli capacity to be raised to Rs.300-500 crore over 1-2 years.
verdicts.note: Acharya: 'this year, we have plan of around INR300 crores, INR350 crores... more than 150 tanks are under construction at our Savli plant'. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Savli capacity-building/infrastructure expansion (incl. cryo shop) will be fully commissioned by end of March 2025, leaving no capacity stress for next year.
verdicts.note: Acharya: 'stabilization will take around 6 months to 1 year' — commissioning done but full stabilization/no-capacity-stress state is still being reached, later than the end-Mar-2025 framing.

verdicts.item: Company plans Rs.80-100 crore capex in FY26 (similar to prior year) and is ready for next 2 years capacity-wise.
verdicts.note: Acharya: 'our Capex for this year, we have targeted around INR80 crores... some expansion of our Kandla facility... Kalol and Savli'. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Company secured its largest-ever LNG order, a turnkey mini-LNG terminal in The Bahamas (15,000 metric ton storage, world's largest double-walled VI LNG tank) to be completed in about 12-14 months.
verdicts.note: Acharya: 'we have been doing the LNG small-scale terminals at Bahamas now, and we already finished at Caribbean LNG' — Bahamas project underway, not yet completed.

verdicts.item: Beverage keg 9-month revenue was ~Rs.19 crore and management expects to end FY25 at ~Rs.30-35 crore (below earlier target); Savli plant total ~Rs.200 crore revenue this year.
verdicts.note: Acharya: 'last year, we did almost INR200 crores from that plant' — the ~Rs.200 cr Savli portion confirmed; the Rs.30-35 cr keg figure is not restated. [±10% rule]

wtt.summary: 46% guidance hit (24 chains); 1/4 projects on-time; 24% theme consistency (info)
wtt.tone_latest: Confident and expansive across all four segments; management reaffirmed 18-20% FY26 growth and downplayed US tariff impact, while candidly acknowledging keg volumes remain below internal expectations and the ITER Cryostat order is a one-off.

risks.note: Top 10 customers contributed 51% of FY26 revenues, creating sensitivity to individual customer demand cycles.

Export revenues comprised 59% of FY26 revenues, exposing the Company to anti-dumping investigations, trade barriers, shipping disruptions and currency volatility in key export markets, as well as trade-policy shifts.

Dependence on four principal manufacturing facilities in India; disruption at a facility could affect production, mitigated by preventive maintenance, business continuity planning and multi-plant redundancy.
Exposure to steel, stainless steel and energy price fluctuations; mitigated by strategic procurement, vendor diversification and selective pass-through pricing in contracts.
Orders are subject to revision, delay or cancellation, which could affect revenue visibility from the order backlog.

risks.risk: Demand cyclicality from long equipment life cycles
risks.note: Major operators periodically relocate existing equipment rather than buy new, deferring procurement and creating episodic demand troughs.

risks.risk: Commodity price and policy sensitivity of LNG/hydrogen demand
risks.note: Future demand for LNG and hydrogen equipment is sensitive to commodity prices and government policy continuity (e.g. India's gas-in-energy-mix and Green Hydrogen Mission targets), both of which carry structural uncertainty.
Increasing competition from low-cost manufacturers in emerging markets offering aggressive pricing on standardised equipment categories.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Growth in air separation plants, semiconductor manufacturing, the hydrogen economy and advanced industrial processes continues to create strong demand for cryogenic storage, transportation and handling solutions
- India's industrial expansion and rising investments in electronics manufacturing, specialty chemicals, steel, pharmaceuticals and healthcare are accelerating the need for reliable cryogenic infrastructure
- Global energy transition initiatives are driving increasing demand for hydrogen, ammonia and other clean energy carriers, creating new opportunities for technologically advanced cryogenic equipment
- Increasing adoption of cryogenic solutions in healthcare, biotechnology, dairy and industrial applications is supporting strong demand for liquid nitrogen containers, liquid cylinders and other standardised equipment
- Growing investments in semiconductor fabrication facilities, renewable energy infrastructure and advanced manufacturing hubs are expanding the scope for engineered cryogenic storage systems
- Government target to raise natural gas' share of India's energy mix from ~6% to 15% by 2030 is accelerating LNG import terminal expansion, City Gas Distribution network growth and LNG fuelling corridor development, expected to significantly increase demand for LNG storage, transportation and regasification systems
- Gradual transition of heavy vehicles towards LNG power (longer range, lower emissions, improved efficiency versus diesel) is expected to drive strong demand for cryogenic fuel tanks and semi-trailers
- The marine sector is increasingly adopting LNG-powered vessels to comply with environmental regulations, creating new opportunities for marine fuel tanks and related LNG infrastructure
- Steel, mining, cement and heavy manufacturing industries are increasingly evaluating LNG as a cleaner fuel alternative for logistics and industrial applications
- EBITDA margin reflects operating leverage benefits on a higher revenue base alongside disciplined cost management
- PBT growth supported by higher operating income and declining finance costs driven by the Company's strong balance sheet
- Order Inflow in FY26 was Rs. 1,685 Cr, up 9.9% YoY, reflecting sustained global demand across the Company's addressable segments
- Order Backlog as at end-FY26 stood at Rs. 1,514 Cr, split approximately 49% Industrial Gas, 28% LNG and 22% Cryo Scientific Division, providing visibility on near-term revenue
- Sold 70+ LNG semi-trailers during the financial year, strengthening presence in LNG logistics solutions
- Executing a third major LNG contract in The Bahamas featuring ten vacuum-insulated tanks with 15,000 cubic metres combined capacity, serving as a regional clean energy hub
- Secured a prestigious order from Cochin Shipyard for 6 units of 800 m3 Marine Fuel Gas Tanks for CMA CGM container vessels, marking entry into Indian shipyards and the largest marine tanks executed by the Company
- Secured export orders for LNG storage tanks, marine fuel gas tanks and LNG infrastructure projects across Asia, Africa and South America
- First-of-a-kind order for largest-size (10 units) horizontal LOX storage tanks under manufacture for a space research company
- First-of-a-kind order for a vertical LH2 storage tank (90kl) from a European customer for a semiconductor/electronics factory

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Higher margins in new products: ultra-purity ammonia and CO2 battery storage (premium pricing); cost pressures mitigated by antidumping duties on Chinese kegs; Savli plant costs front-loaded (stabilizing by Q4FY26); steel tariff impact on US cylinders limited to material cost only (50% of price), EBIT margin remains 14-15%

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing capex for LNG and keg capacity; maintaining net cash position (INR275cr available); no dividend or buyback mentioned; focus on organic growth and strategic order execution

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Targeted investments in advanced automation and precision fabrication strengthened manufacturing capabilities during FY26, enhancing throughput and ensuring adherence to global quality standards, positioning the Company's facilities as competitive export hubs for complex, high-value infrastructure. The Kandla (KASEZ) export-oriented facility was honoured with the Award for Excellence in Export 2024-25. Capital expenditure allocated toward enhancement of sustainability and safety measures represented 5.65% of total capex in FY26 (6.29% in FY25), per BRSR Principle 2 disclosure.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Highly confident, forward-looking, and execution-focused; emphasized technological leadership, global approvals, and policy tailwinds; tone on LNG and kegs is bullish; ITER and CO2 battery framed as strategic differentiators, not one-offs

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Global leader in customised cryogenic equipment; among the largest cryogenic tank manufacturers in the world
- Complete end-to-end capability: design, engineering, manufacturing, installation and after-sales service
- Diversified customer base of 590+ clients across industrial gas, LNG, scientific and beverage segments
- Export-oriented manufacturing at Kandla Special Economic Zone providing logistics and duty advantages for international business
- International commercial infrastructure: subsidiaries and service centres in Brazil, marketing offices in Europe
- Backward and forward integration with group companies contributing 10% of revenues
- Robust financial profile: Debt-Equity of 0.06x (FY26), interest coverage of 38.04x, RONW of 23.08%

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Keg volume ramp-up delayed vs internal targets; LNG station rollout slower than policy potential; execution risk on ITER project (long duration); global trade policy shifts (US tariffs); competitive pressure from Chinese players in kegs (mitigated by antidumping duties)

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The INR28,000cr Q2FY26 keg order (pre-announced) is likely a cumulative pipeline value, not a single order — indicating strong pre-commitments from global brewers; ITER’s 200 CTS panels represent a multi-year, high-margin, repeatable workstream beyond the INR145cr order; CO2 battery order from Italy signals export-ready clean energy tech, not just domestic

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Order intake] "Highest ever Order booking" of Rs 532 Cr in Q1FY27 (Actual orders received Rs 532 Cr vs Rs 415 Cr in Q1FY26, +28.4%), which the deck notes "includes high value order of Rs 217 Cr from US major private Aerospace Co. (IG)"; the Q1FY26 base included an ITER France order of Rs 146 Cr for CTS Repair (CSD). Q1FY27 order mix: IG 72%, LNG 16%, CSD 10%, Other 2%.
- [Aerospace / space] Secured AS9100 Aerospace Certification serving aviation, space and defence; an additional order from a US space company for large size (1000M3) tanks and a high-value repeat order from a global aerospace company; the 2024 milestone records an order for largest size (1500M3) tanks in the IG segment from a US space company. The deck also details INOXCVA's role in ISRO test-facility and launchpad systems.
- [Big science] Secured an order for 22 Nos of cryogenic modules for CERN's HL-LHC project, plus an additional ITER order for installation of Cryo & Warm line and refurbishment of the Lower Cryostat Thermal Shield; ITER First Plasma is cited as expected in 2035 and India is described as developing a 25-year fusion roadmap with two new tokamak machines before an Indian DEMO in the late 2040s.
- [Partnerships] Agreement with Wayout to explore a freshwater infra system for the Asian market, and a collaboration with ITMBU for skill development in orbital welding and semiconductor industries; India's semiconductor push (ISM) is flagged as an adjacent opportunity.
- [Headwind stated] "Sales were marginally lower on YoY basis primarily due to ongoing logistics disruptions arising from the geopolitical situation involving Iran and the Gulf region"; other income also fell 14.7% as forex gain dropped to Rs 0.3 Cr from Rs 2.9 Cr.

one-line thesis: INOX India delivered strong Q1FY26 growth with 16.7% revenue rise, driven by breakthrough orders in ultra-high-purity ammonia containers and India’s first CO2 battery storage system, while LNG and keg segments show scalable momentum; the company’s diversified high-margin product portfolio and strategic capex expansion position it to capture India’s clean energy transition and global industrial supply chain reshoring.
financial scorecard: revenue: +16.7% YoY; EBITDA/margin: +19.4% YoY, margin improved from 23.1% to 25.3% (excludes one-off other income of INR12.5cr from reversal of prior provisions); PAT (rptd): +18.9% YoY; PAT (normalized): +15.2% YoY (excluding INR12.5cr other income); order book: INR1,457cr as of Jun 30, 2025 (45% IG, 32% LNG, 23% Cryo); net debt: INR275cr fund availability (net cash position)
guidance: revenue growth: 18-20% YoY; margin: stable EBITDA margin target of ~25%; order inflow: expects strong Q2-Q4 inflow from LNG, Cryo, and keg segments; capex/commissioning: INR80cr total capex for FY26, including INR5-6cr for LNG tank capacity expansion at Kalol, Savli plant stabilization by Q4FY26
order book & pipeline: INR1,457cr as of Jun 30, 2025; 63% export content; major components: INR145cr ITER Cryostat Thermal Shield order (2-year duration), 11 ultra-high-purity ammonia containers (2 delivered, 9 in production), 145 LNG fuel tanks dispatched, 28,000cr keg orders received in Q2FY26 (pre-announced)
segment / subsidiary detail: Industrial Gas: 48% of revenue; led by ultra-high-purity ammonia containers (first in India, 11 units ordered) and CO2 battery storage (first order, 26 units); LNG: 29% of revenue; 145 tanks dispatched, capacity expansion to 5,000-6,000 tanks/year by end-FY26; Cryo Scientific: 19% of revenue; INR145cr ITER order (90% in-house fabrication); Beverage Kegs: low base but accelerating; 6.4cr Q1 orders, Q2 FY26 orders at INR28,000cr (pre-announced), global approvals from Heineken & AB InBev secured, Asahi/Carlsberg audits scheduled for Sep-Oct 2025
growth verticals / optionality: LNG fueling station ecosystem (Adani/Ambani land conversion policy), SMR nuclear reactor manufacturing (bidding with govt partners), hydrogen equipment scaling, CO2 battery commercialization (global replication potential), keg volume ramp-up (3-4x current size target by FY28)
margins & cost dynamics: Higher margins in new products: ultra-purity ammonia and CO2 battery storage (premium pricing); cost pressures mitigated by antidumping duties on Chinese kegs; Savli plant costs front-loaded (stabilizing by Q4FY26); steel tariff impact on US cylinders limited to material cost only (50% of price), EBIT margin remains 14-15%
capex / expansion: INR80cr total for FY26; INR5-6cr for LNG tank capacity expansion at Kalol; capex for Kandla (1,500m³ vessels) and Savli plant upgrades; no new greenfield announced yet, scaling via brownfield expansion
capital allocation: Prioritizing capex for LNG and keg capacity; maintaining net cash position (INR275cr available); no dividend or buyback mentioned; focus on organic growth and strategic order execution
risks & watch-items: Keg volume ramp-up delayed vs internal targets; LNG station rollout slower than policy potential; execution risk on ITER project (long duration); global trade policy shifts (US tariffs); competitive pressure from Chinese players in kegs (mitigated by antidumping duties)
management quality / tone: Highly confident, forward-looking, and execution-focused; emphasized technological leadership, global approvals, and policy tailwinds; tone on LNG and kegs is bullish; ITER and CO2 battery framed as strategic differentiators, not one-offs
non-obvious takeaways: The INR28,000cr Q2FY26 keg order (pre-announced) is likely a cumulative pipeline value, not a single order — indicating strong pre-commitments from global brewers; ITER’s 200 CTS panels represent a multi-year, high-margin, repeatable workstream beyond the INR145cr order; CO2 battery order from Italy signals export-ready clean energy tech, not just domestic
